description: Starter mapping between common cloud scanner (CSPM-style) finding types and CCC-2:2024 control IDs. This is a best-effort starting ruleset, not an NCA-endorsed mapping — review each entry against ccc_controls.json and your own finding taxonomy, then adjust. control_ids reference the 'id' field in ccc_controls.json domains[].subdomains[].controls[].
how_to_use: Tag each finding your scanner emits with a finding_type matching one of the keys below. Your rules engine looks up ccc_controls_csp / ccc_controls_cst depending on whether the scanned target is CSP-owned infrastructure or a CST's cloud account, then attaches those control IDs (and pulls the human-readable text from ccc_controls.json) to the finding for reporting.

findings.title: SSH (22/tcp) open to 0.0.0.0/0
RDP (3389/tcp) open to 0.0.0.0/0
Security group / NSG allows unrestricted inbound traffic
Object storage bucket is publicly readable
findings.domain: 2-6 Data and Information Protection / 2-2 Identity and Access Management
findings.notes: No CCC subcontrol names 'public bucket' directly — this is a best-effort mapping to the closest access-control and confidentiality controls; refine to your own risk taxonomy.

findings.title: Object storage bucket is publicly writable
findings.domain: 2-6 Data and Information Protection / 2-2 Identity and Access Management

findings.title: Object/block storage without encryption at rest
Data transmitted without TLS/encryption
No MFA enforced on privileged/admin account
Root/master account used for routine operations instead of scoped IAM roles
Password policy does not meet complexity/rotation baseline
findings.notes: CCC largely defers detailed password rules to ECC 2-2; this finding is also relevant to your ECC ruleset if you maintain one.

findings.title: IAM policy grants wildcard (*) resource/action permissions
Audit/activity logging disabled on a resource or account
findings.domain: 2-11 Cybersecurity Event Logs and Monitoring Management

findings.title: No centralized monitoring/SIEM ingestion configured
findings.domain: 2-11 Cybersecurity Event Logs and Monitoring Management

findings.title: No backup configured for a critical resource
findings.notes: CCC only defines backup subcontrols on the CSP side. For CST-owned resources, treat this as an ECC backup-domain finding rather than CCC-CST.

findings.title: Backup exists but is unencrypted or not access-restricted
Cryptographic key without a rotation policy
Hardcoded secrets/keys found in code or configuration
findings.domain: 2-2 Identity and Access Management / 2-16 System Development Security

findings.title: Known CVE / missing patch on a cloud workload or image
No recurring vulnerability scanning configured
Public-facing web application without WAF / transaction protection
findings.notes: Web application security is CSP-only in CCC's scope; for a CST-built app on top of IaaS, also map to ECC's web application security domain.

findings.title: No documented disaster recovery / business continuity plan for a critical service
Third-party/marketplace service used without security documentation or review
findings.notes: CCC only defines a third-party subdomain on the CSP side; for CST-side vendor risk, fall back to ECC's third-party cybersecurity domain.

findings.title: Storage media disposed of or reused without a sanitization process
findings.notes: Physical media handling is CSP-only in CCC. Related CST finding: end-user device sanitization maps to 2-5-T-1-1.

findings.title: No session timeout / lockout enforced on a management console
No capability to forcibly terminate an active remote/admin session
